name: slow
title: SLOW — timelocked transfers with a reverse
description: The SLOW dapp as one self-contained HTML document, served from contract bytecode over ERC-8244, ERC-5219 and ERC-4804.

protocol.note: 0x0000...AaBC is v1, live on Ethereum and named by the page until the redeployment lands. The build being deployed is src/SLOW.sol; v1's source is src/SLOWv1.sol. See `deployment` for the address it goes to.

verified.permissioned: Salt bytes[0:20] are the steward, so only that address reaches this contract address. A different sender deploying the same salt lands elsewhere (checked: 0x8179a1CE...).
verified.chainIndependent: Salt byte[20] is CreateX's redeploy-protection flag and MUST stay 0x00. Setting it mixes block.chainid into the guarded salt and yields three different addresses.
verified.method: Simulated CreateX.deployCreate3 as the steward on all three chains; identical result. scripts/address.mjs reproduces it offline via createxAddress().

bridge.note: SlowArrival and SlowRelay, CREATE3 through the same steward and deployer as the page. Addresses derived before deployment and checked free on all three chains.

constructorArgs: message deliverers: both on chain 1, none on an L2

verified.method: test/DeployBridgeFork.t.sol runs the live CreateX on forks of 1, 8453 and 4663 with DIFFERENT constructor arguments on each and asserts one address. scripts/address.mjs reproduces the derivation offline.
verified.whyItMatters: SlowRelay.receiveRelay accepts a proof only when the recovered origin equals address(this). Diverging addresses would stop settlement silently.
